body:
We chased this same bug on macOS 27.0 (26A428) while moving our app to beta.24, and landed on a different root cause. Sharing the probe data in case it saves you a round trip.

**beta.24 already fixes it.** wailsapp/wails#5919 (closing #5752) merged 2026-08-28 and ships in beta.24 as `systemTrayCoerceEventType` at `systemtray_darwin.m:14-22`. We bumped to mainline beta.24 and left-click works correctly on 27 — verified by hand, plus an `AXPress` probe that opens the menu and enumerates its items.

Worth double-checking your version: the issue body says beta.24, but System Details says beta.9. beta.9 predates the fix, which would explain the symptom.

**The target/action diagnosis does not match what we measured.** We instrumented `systemtray_darwin.m` on 27 and logged every hop. The action handler *does* fire on left-click, and both targets were already correct at creation:

```
action-fired currentEvent=NSEvent: type=KitDefined ... type=13 pressedMouseButtons=1
go systrayClickCallback buttonID= 13
go processClick b= 13 menu==nil: false      <- matches no case, silently drops
```

So `statusItemClicked:` is reached. What breaks is `[NSApp currentEvent]` at action time: on 27 it reports `NSEventTypeAppKitDefined (13)` or `NSEventTypeMouseMoved (5)` instead of `NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown (1)`, so `processClick`'s switch matches nothing and the click evaporates with no error. Right-click still reports `NSEventTypeRightMouseDown (3)` correctly, which is the asymmetry. That is exactly what #5919 coerces: raw 13/5 with the right-button bit unset becomes `NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown`.

There is a second layer #5919 does not fix, which may be what you are seeing if you are genuinely on beta.24. The local event monitor never receives left-mouse-down on 27 because `event.window` is a `WebviewWindow` rather than the `NSStatusBarWindow`, so the `event.window != button.window` guard at `systemtray_darwin.m:61` rejects it:

```
monitor-fired type=1 event.window=<WebviewWindow: 0x7721c7d680>
                     button.window=<NSStatusBarWindow: 0x7721628500> match=0
monitor-rejected-by-window-guard type=1
```

Left-click therefore reaches the menu through the synthesized-mouseDown path in `showMenu()` rather than the monitor. It works, but it is a route around the problem rather than a fix.

None of this makes your change wrong — moving target/action onto `statusItem.button` is correct modern API and matches Apple's current guidance, since `NSStatusItem.target`/`action` are now documented as applying only when using a custom view rather than `-button`. It just was not the cause of the dropped click for us.

See also #5760, which replaces the local event monitors with gesture recognizers per TN3212 and the synthesized event with `performClick:`. That is the direction Apple's macOS 27 SDK points: `NSStatusItemExpandedInterfaceSession` says it "should be used instead of manually toggling your interface by target/action handling on the button or item".
@jasikpark thanks a lot for the update, will test with the beta version you mentioned. Closed my PR.
@jasikpark thanks a lot, using the latest code works!
